At 0% progress, prioritize a small, testable architectural change: **zero-initialized recent-history pooling alongside SASRec**, accompanied by controlled history diagnostics. No improvement is established yet.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Feedback identifies broad relatedness crowding out specific next choices, motivating a recency experiment without establishing its cause. (2) Training margins cannot establish validation gains or useful history dependence. (3) Compatibility and redundancy claims require explicit evidence; histories cannot establish ownership or continuing demand.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [Recency research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722) cautions against excessive recent-item emphasis. (2) [FCESR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.13632) distinguishes sufficiency from necessity, motivating matched retention/deletion probes without equating dependence with intent. (3) [Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) establish sampled-ranking inconsistencies; retain the pinned metric and qualify broader claims. (4) [SASRec](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/model.py) and [ReZero](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04887) motivate preserving embedding scales and using exact baseline-equivalent initialization.

**Framework and directions.**

| Layer | Existing approach | Proposed addition | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Prediction | SASRec sequence features | Zero-initialized recent residual | Recent activity may be incidental |
| Dependence | Training margins | Matched deletion and retention | Dependence does not establish intent |
| Interpretation | Metadata breakdowns | Source-supported flags and abstention | Ownership and prerequisites remain uncertain |

**Candidate ideas and assessments.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

1. **Recent-history residual — 3/6/3.** Originality: inspectable combination, but established components. Potential: cheap and ablatable, but may duplicate SASRec. Difficulty: small change, but export parity matters.
2. **Matched history perturbations — 4/6/4.** Originality: task-specific controls, but established methods. Potential: exposes dependence, but does not improve ranking directly. Difficulty: hooks suffice, but positional effects require care.
3. **Evidence-backed rejection flags — 5/6/6.** Originality: connects feedback to spans, but resembles rule-based verification. Potential: actionable diagnosis, but limited coverage. Difficulty: feasible extraction, but brittle specification matching.

**Selected algorithm.** Compute baseline features h and the causal, non-padding weighted mean p of the last k=5 input item embeddings, decay=0.7. Use z=h+αp, initializing learned per-dataset α=0. Preserve baseline embedding scales, loss, optimizer and seeds. Unlike the previous sigmoid(-4) plus extra LayerNorm proposal, this preserves initial scores exactly; mixing strength still depends on feature norms.

```python
h = sasrec(sequence)
p = causal_recent_pool(item_emb(sequence), k=5, decay=0.7)
z = mask_padding(h + alpha * p)  # alpha starts at zero
logits = baseline_candidate_dot(z, item_emb(candidates))
```

Compare unchanged baseline and residual first; conditionally examine normalization-only, pooling-only and combined variants. The former sigmoid(-4)/extra-normalization design remains a comparator, not an equivalent initialization. Uniform pooling, last-item, raw/√d-scaled pools, fixed/learned gates and scalar-temperature controls are follow-ups subject to budget. Log norms, gates, gradients and logit spread. Examine popularity/history-length slices and matched perturbations for shortcuts; distinguish inference sensitivity from retrained ablations.

Predeclare checkpoint rules, validation frequency and trial limits; select only pinned macro validation HR@10. Paired within-category bootstrap intervals exclude training variation and selection bias. Preserve all four routes, splits, seeds, DATA_DIR and trial-local artifacts. Retain DiagnosisProbe’s interface, actual model reference, residual-enhanced features and consistent scoring; unavailable category lists remain empty. Bound diagnostics, retain twenty-user full-catalog recommendations, and verify exported scores/rankings. Treat simulator feedback and repeatedly selected validation gains as exploratory.

idea.description: Add a zero-initialized learned residual from causal recent-history embedding pooling to each SASRec sequence feature, independently for all four dataset models. Replace the originally proposed sigmoid gate and extra LayerNorm in the primary experiment so initialization exactly preserves baseline scores.
idea.motivation: Qualitative feedback motivates testing whether recent observed activity supplies additional predictive evidence, but it does not establish recency as the cause of failures. A minimal residual permits a controlled experiment. Zero initialization avoids confounding the intervention with a fresh normalization layer or immediate score changes; it does not guarantee improved ranking or intent alignment.

Respect SASREC_EPOCHS=200 from the environment and baseline overrides. Use k=5 and decay=0.7 initially; alpha is one unconstrained scalar per dataset, initialized to zero, and may become negative. Pool raw item embeddings before positional embeddings/dropout; preserve the baseline's existing sequence-input scaling, candidate embeddings, final normalization and scoring. Do not insert an additional LayerNorm in the primary variant. Pool only events at or before each prediction position, with zero-padding masks and no wraparound. Because normalized pooling averages vectors, its norm can be much smaller than the sequence feature norm; record pool/feature norm ratios, alpha, alpha gradients, effective residual norms and logit spread. A zero alpha initially blocks residual-branch embedding gradients but permits learning alpha when its loss gradient is nonzero. Preserve baseline model initialization and RNG consumption: add the scalar without random initialization, reuse identical baseline weights for initial equivalence checks, and use separate diagnostic RNG streams. First compare unchanged baseline against the residual under matched training settings and tuning effort; alpha fixed at zero is an implementation equivalence control, not evidence of a separate mechanism. If justified by remaining budget, compare LN_extra(h), h+g*p and LN_extra(h+g*p), including the former sigmoid gate initialized at -4. Its initial gate is about 0.018, and extra LayerNorm is not baseline-equivalent. Raw versus sqrt(d)-scaled pools, fixed versus learned gates, and baseline score-temperature controls distinguish representation effects from loss-scale effects. Unknown prerequisites remain unknown; diagnostic abstention must not suppress recommendations. For perturbations, match deletion counts, account for padding and position shifts, and separate inference-time sensitivity from retrained controls. idea.pseudocode:
class RecentResidualSASRec(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, baseline):
        super().__init__()
        self.sasrec = baseline
        self.alpha = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(()))
        # Access item_emb through baseline; avoid duplicate module registration.

    @property
    def item_emb(self):
        return self.sasrec.item_emb

    def log2feats(self, sequence):
        h = self.sasrec.log2feats(sequence)
        embeddings = self.item_emb(sequence)
        numerator = zeros_like(embeddings)
        denominator = zeros_like(sequence, dtype=embeddings.dtype)
        # shift_right inserts zeros and never wraps around.
        for offset in range(5):
            shifted_ids = shift_right(sequence, offset)
            shifted_emb = shift_right(embeddings, offset)
            weight = (0.7 ** offset) * (shifted_ids != 0)
            numerator += shifted_emb * weight[..., None]
            denominator += weight
        recent = numerator / denominator.clamp_min(1)[..., None]
        features = h + self.alpha * recent
        return features * (sequence != 0)[..., None]

    def predict_score(self, features, items):
        # Preserve baseline candidate broadcasting, scaling and any scoring terms.
        return self.sasrec.predict_score(features, items)

# Ensure forward/training uses this wrapper's log2feats, not baseline.forward.
# Train with the unchanged baseline loss and optimizer, including alpha.
# Instantiate four independent dataset models; preserve dataset routing.
# Before training: copy baseline weights, set eval mode, assert matching
# non-padding features and candidate scores at alpha=0.
# Select only with the pinned macro validation HR@10 and declared checkpoint rules.
# Export the exact wrapper/configuration through the predictor writer.
# Reload selected checkpoints and verify scores, rankings, masks and routing.
# Keep diagnostics bounded and record all GPU time against the shared budget.

originality.positive: Combines an explicit recency branch with baseline-equivalent initialization and controlled diagnostic comparisons.
originality.negative: Recency pooling, scalar residual gates and zero-initialized residuals are established techniques; this is an incremental application.

future_potential.positive: Provides an inexpensive foundation for testing when recent history adds predictive information across categories.
future_potential.negative: It may duplicate SASRec, exploit popularity or last-item shortcuts, and cannot directly resolve compatibility, redundancy or latent intent.

code_difficulty.positive: The primary model change requires causal pooling and one scalar parameter per dataset.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct training integration, masking, export parity and controlled comparisons require more care than the short formula suggests.

related_work.title: Measuring Recency Bias (2024)
contributions: Provides evidence that excessive recent-item emphasis can hurt recommendation accuracy.
Motivates measuring recency effects rather than assuming they are beneficial.
limitations: Does not establish gains from this residual on the four RecHarness datasets.
Recency sensitivity does not identify user intent.

related_work.title: FCESR (2025)
contributions: Distinguishes recommendation sufficiency from necessity.
Motivates complementary retention and deletion probes.
limitations: Model dependence does not establish perceived intent.
Perturbations require controls for deletion count, padding and positional shifts.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Establishes that sampled evaluation can change model ordering, even in expectation.
Supports limiting claims made from the pinned sampled benchmark.
limitations: Does not justify changing the host evaluation protocol.
Repeated candidate draws do not eliminate systematic sampling bias.

related_work.title: SASRec: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation (2018), original implementation
contributions: Documents sequence-input embedding scaling and final normalization before candidate scoring.
Provides the architectural reference for distinguishing pooling, normalization and score-scale effects.
limitations: The RecHarness implementation must retain its actual conventions; the original repository does not establish exact template behavior.
Original baseline comparisons do not validate the proposed decayed-pooling residual.

related_work.title: ReZero is All You Need: Fast Convergence at Large Depth
contributions: Introduces zero-initialized residual gates.
Supports exact initial preservation of a pre-existing feature path when adding an additive branch.
limitations: Does not establish recommendation gains or an optimal gate constraint.
Baseline equivalence also requires unchanged surrounding normalization, scoring and initialization.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how repeated model selection can overfit validation criteria.
Motivates predeclared trial limits and complete validation-query records.
limitations: A small search does not eliminate selection bias.
Conditional paired bootstrap intervals do not account for adaptive model selection.

related_work.title: Do Sequential Recommendation Benchmarks Require Higher-Order Sequence Modelling? (2026)
contributions: Reports strong pairwise-history controls against Transformer recommenders under shared splits.
Motivates last-item, transition and simple history-pooling comparisons.
limitations: Its Amazon categories differ from this task.
It does not directly establish the proposed exponentially decayed embedding-pooling control.

related_work.title: Sequence or Pseudo-Sequence? (2021)
contributions: Reports limited SASRec changes under shuffled training histories in studied settings.
Motivates distinguishing chronological dependence from simpler history signals.
limitations: Findings need not transfer to these datasets.
Inference shuffling and retraining on shuffled histories answer different questions.

related_work.title: SciPy paired bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents paired resampling of aligned observations.
Supports paired user comparisons within categories, followed by equal category averaging.
limitations: Intervals condition on the observed trained models and fixed candidate sets.
They exclude training-seed variability and repeated-selection bias.

related_work.title: PyTorch numerical accuracy documentation
contributions: Explains why mathematically equivalent computations may differ numerically.
Motivates recording precision/backend settings and checking exported inference.
limitations: Numerical tolerances alone do not guarantee identical top-10 rankings.
Export discrepancies still require investigation when they affect selection or prediction.
